verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'As their spacecraft slipped into Earth’s atmosphere ... on Friday'; R2: context of Flight Day 10 on April 10, 2026; R3: 'April 10 ... re-entry'; R4: 'April 10 ... re-entry'; R5: 'April 10, 2026 ... reenter Earth's atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm re-entry on Friday, April 10, 2026, matching date, day, and event.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule's entry interface occurred around 7:53 p.m. EDT (4:53 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'At 7:53 p.m., ... “entry interface”'; R2: '7:53 p.m.: ... entry interface'; R3: 'Around 7:53 p.m. ET ... entry interface'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state entry interface at 7:53 p.m. ET/EDT; PDT conversion matches 3-hour difference.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time ... off San Diego'; R2: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'; R3: '5:07 p.m. local time ... off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashed down ... at 5.07pm PT ... Pacific Ocean'; R5: '8:07 p.m. ET ... off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm exact location, time in EDT/PDT, and Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule's splashdown marked the end of the crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'successful conclusion of Artemis II'; R2: 'completing the Artemis II crew’s return to Earth'; R3: 'successfully recovered after splashdown'; R4: 'the mission is over'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe splashdown as completing the mission and crew's return, directly supporting it as the end.

verifications.claim: The communication blackout lasted approximately 6 minutes starting at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'blackout ... for six minutes' at '7:53 p.m.'; R2: 'six-minute communications blackout' at '7:53 p.m.'; R3: 'six-minute communication blackout' at '7:53 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely match 6-minute blackout starting at 7:53 p.m. EDT/ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule's drogue chutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. EDT at 22,000 ft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '22,000 feet ... drogues deployed'; R2: '8:03 p.m.: Around 22,000 feet ... drogue parachutes'; R3: '8:03 p.m. ET, the drogue parachutes'
verifications.reasoning: Direct matches for time and altitude in sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule's main chutes deployed at 8:04 p.m. EDT at 6,000 ft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'main parachutes ... a minute later' after drogues; R2: '8:04 p.m.: At around 6,000 feet ... main parachutes'; R3: 'main parachute ... at 8:04'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm exact time and altitude for main chute deployment.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule traveled at over 24,000 mph during its entry into the atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'more than 24,000 miles per hour ... entry'; 'peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour'; R3: 'peak velocity of 24,664 mph'; '23,000 to 25,000 mph'; 'nearly 25,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state speeds over 24,000 mph during atmospheric entry.

verifications.claim: Over 24,000 mph is roughly 35 times the speed of sound.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'traveling nearly 35 times the speed of sound' at entry (context of ~24,000+ mph)
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly equates entry speed to nearly 35 times speed of sound, matching claim.
